title: Movie buffs: How do you creatively engage with film beyond just watching?

commenti.body: I run a movie club with over 1K members. We watch movies, have discussions, do movie trivia nights, happy hours, etc. I also do my own illustrations of scenes/characters from my favorite films. I turn some of them into T-shirt/sticker designs.
Wow. You can't just say that without giving more details. Is there a discord channel for your movie club? How did your essays used to perform?

I host a weekly movie club in my ultra low budget home theater.  It's only about 6-10 of us depending on the night.  We pick a theme or genre and then select 10 films that fit that theme, usually ending on a parody.  I create a write-up for each film, usually a couple paragraphs depending on how I'm feeing, and post it into a FB group a couple days beforehand and anyone who feels like showing up is welcome.
That's the dream. To find friends with similar taste in film. I only have friends that say "I won't like it if you do" lmao.

I'd like to think that film - and art, in general - gives me inspiration for my own creative endeavours. I'm an academic in the humanities, and I've long held that the kind of writing we do is in some senses more akin to a piece of literature than to the kinds of papers my friends in the Empirical fields write. Moreover, I've always thought of art is a lifeblood to the academic.

Its hard to really point at thing it has given me for my writing: I think a formal understanding of the three-act structure had encouraged me to get to the heart of things in my essays that bit earlier, rather than dwell too long on prefacing things. I've structured pieces of writing more thematically, in a manner that at the time reminded me most of works of art like DW Griffiths' *Intolerance*. I'm fond of epigraphs and allusions, and so certain films come in handy.

Write about them. Talk to people about them. Read about them.

Then I decided that wasn't enough and took a screenwriting class. Now I read the screenplays and am starting the journey of learning how to write them for myself.
Love the perspective. I take away that even if we are not directly contributing to the film community, our love for it can have ripple effects that positively influence our other endeavors. Amazing.

I actually find having too similar taste to also run against good discussion. One of my best friends I can trust for recommendations, just like I'll recommend things to him. Another friend dislikes a lot of things I like, while I like things they don't. Not genre-wise, but more to do with tropes. I love discussing with both, but when talking with the second friend I walk away thinking about the movie a lot more. I feel more challenged.

I'd say most of us are open to trying out new movies more than we have similar tastes exactly.  I've definitely shown a couple where not everyone enjoyed it.  I've been doing this for about 4 years now and what I've found is that you really need to mix it up to keep it fun and keep people coming back.  For a while, everything was art-house but that kind of got a bit exhausting.  So now I try to mix it up and throw in stuff like Face/Off or Godzilla vs Mothra, depending on the theme, something we can just have fun hanging out and riffing on.  For the past couple months we've been slowly going through a "Best of Bond" and that's been a blast.
I've heard people having dedicated months in a year for certain themes. Jan for classics, Feb for Romance for example. Keeps it fresh but you still know what to expect.
